| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἐπιθαρσύνων (τὸν δ’ ἐπιθαρσύνων προσέφη ξανθὸς Μενέλαος, 4.183) | "Him, cheering on, addressed fair-haired Menelaus:" | "Fair-haired Menelaus said to him, cheering him on:" | "encouraging", "heartening", "reassuring"; θαρσύνω keeps the Odyssey’s "cheer" (12.360); ξανθός "fair-haired" and προσέφη as in the table (odyssey 15.110) |
| θάρσει (4.184) | "Take courage" | "Take courage" | "Take heart" (θυμός is "heart"), "Be bold", "Fear not"; θάρσος is "courage" in the Odyssey table |

| ἐν καιρίῳ (4.185) | "in a vital place" | "in a vital place" | "in a mortal spot", "in a deadly place", "at a fatal point"; καίριος "in the right place", of wounds "vital" |

| εἰρύσατο (4.186; ἐρύομαι "protect, ward") | "guarded (me)" | "guarded me" | "warded off" (reserved for ἀμύνω), "saved", "shielded"; ἔρυμα "protection" in the table’s μίτρη row |

| ζῶμα (4.187, 4.216) | "the waistcloth" | "the waistcloth" | "girdle" (kept for ζώνη, as in ἐϋζώνοιο "well-girdled" and the Odyssey’s καλλίζωνος "fair-girdled"), "apron" and "waist-guard" (turned down for μίτρη), "loin-cloth"; LSJ "girdle, loin-cloth", worn under the belt |
| τὴν χαλκῆες κάμον ἄνδρες (4.187 = 4.216) | "which bronzesmiths toiled to make, men." | "which men, smiths of bronze, toiled to make." | "which bronze-workers fashioned", "which skilled craftsmen made" (adds skill); κάμνω "toil", with ἄνδρες in apposition to χαλκῆες kept in both layers |
| αἲ γὰρ δὴ οὕτως εἴη (4.189) | "Would that it were so indeed" | "If only it were so indeed" | "May it be so", "Would it were so"; follows the table’s αἴθ’ "Would that" / "If only" and the Odyssey’s αἲ γὰρ … "would that" / "if only" (21.200) |

| Ταλθύβιον θεῖον κήρυκα (4.192) | "Talthybius, the divine herald" | "Talthybius, the divine herald" | "godlike", "noble" (θεῖος keeps "divine", as in the Odyssey’s θεῖον ἀοιδόν "the divine minstrel"), "the worthy herald" |

| βὰν δ’ ἰέναι καθ’ ὅμιλον ἀνὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν (4.209) | "And they set out to go down through the throng, up through the wide army of the Achaeans." | "And they set out to go through the throng, up and down the wide army of the Achaeans." | "crowd" (kept for οὐλαμός, 4.251), "host"; βῆ δ’ ἰέναι "set out to go" / "set out" as in the Odyssey (7.298); κατά "down", ἀνά "up" in `l`, "up and down" in `i`; εὐρὺν στρατόν "the wide army" as at 1.478 |

| κρητῆρι κέρωνται (4.260) | "mix in the mixing-bowl" | "mix … in the mixing-bowl" | "blend in the bowl"; κεράννυμι "mix", κρητήρ "mixing-bowl" (Odyssey 4.615) |
| δαιτρὸν πίνωσιν (4.262; sense of δαιτρόν not certain) | "drink their allotted portion" | "drink their allotted portion" | "drink their share", "drink in moderation", "drink the carved portions"; the usual explanation |
| σὸν δὲ πλεῖον δέπας αἰεὶ ἕστηχ’ (4.262–263) | "your cup, full, always stands" | "your cup stands always full" | "is always filled", "your full goblet" (reserved for ἄλεισον), "stands ready"; δέπας "cup" (the Odyssey’s δέπας ἀμφικύπελλον "double cup"), πλεῖον "full" |
| ὅτε θυμὸς ἀνώγοι (4.263) | "whenever the heart bids" | "whenever your heart bids" | "whenever you wish", "your spirit"; θυμός "heart", ἄνωγα "bid" |
| ἀλλ’ ὄρσευ πόλεμον δ’ οἷος πάρος εὔχεαι εἶναι (4.264) | "But rouse yourself to war, such as you formerly boast to be." | "But rouse yourself for war, and be the man you have always boasted that you are." | "pray" (εὔχομαι with an infinitive is "claim, boast", as at 1.396–397), "vow"; ὄρσευ = ὄρσεο, as ὄρσ’ in 4.204; πόλεμόνδε "to war" with the suffix -δε |
| Κρητῶν ἀγός (4.265) | "leader of the Cretans" | "leader of the Cretans" | "captain", "chief" (reserved for ὄρχαμος), "lord" (reserved for κρείων); ἀγός "leader" (ἄγω "lead") |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Ἰδομενεὺς Κρητῶν ἀγὸς ἀντίον ηὔδα (4.265, whole-line reply-formula) | "To him in turn Idomeneus, leader of the Cretans, spoke, face to face:" | "Then Idomeneus, leader of the Cretans, spoke to him in turn, face to face:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); follows iliad-018 (203) and the Odyssey’s τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ … ἀντίον ηὔδα pattern |
| ἐρίηρος ἑταῖρος (4.266) | "a trusty companion" | "your trusty companion" | "faithful", "loyal", "dear" (ἐρίηρος "trusty" in the Odyssey table: ἐρίηρες ἑταῖροι "trusty companions", 9.100); the sense of ἐρίηρος is not fully known |
| μάλα μέν τοι (4.266) | "very much, indeed" | "most surely" | "very truly", "truly", "I assure you"; μάλα "greatly", μέν τοι a stressing particle |
| ὑπέστην καὶ κατένευσα (4.267) | "I undertook and nodded assent" | "I undertook at the first and nodded my assent" | "promised and agreed", "swore and nodded"; ὑφίσταμαι "undertake", κατανεύω "nod assent" |
| ἄλλους ὄτρυνε κάρη κομόωντας Ἀχαιούς (4.268) | "the others urge on, the long-haired-of-head Achaeans" | "urge on the other long-haired Achaeans" | "rouse", "stir up"; ὀτρύνω "urge on" (4.73); κάρη κομόωντες "long-haired" as at 2.50 |
| σύν γ’ ὅρκι’ ἔχευαν (4.269; συγχέω, tmesis) | "they poured the oaths together" | "have thrown the oaths into confusion" | "broken the oaths" (the plain word is reserved for the sense), "confounded", "violated"; σύν … χέω "pour together"; the note explains the figure |
| κήδε’ ὀπίσσω (4.270) | "troubles hereafter" | "troubles … afterwards" | "sorrows", "cares", "woes"; κῆδος "trouble, care" as in the Odyssey’s κήδεα; ὀπίσσω "hereafter, afterwards" |
| θάνατος καὶ κήδε’ ὀπίσσω ἔσσετ’ (4.270–271) | "death and troubles hereafter will be" | "death and troubles will come to them afterwards" | "will befall", "await them"; ἔσσεται "will be" |
